title: Tele-neurological outpatient care in Brandenburg and Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania
summary:
Many rural areas in Brandenburg and Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania have too few neurologists. Many practices are unable to find successors, and patients often have to travel long distances to see specialists. This can lead to diseases such as Parkinson's, multiple sclerosis, or epilepsy being diagnosed too late or not treated optimally.

TENEAM aims to close this gap. The project connects general practitioners, neurologists, and university hospitals via telemedicine.
Patients who cannot get an appointment at a local neurologist's office within three weeks can be connected to a neurologist via video consultation at their general practitioner's office or, if necessary, from home. Using special telemedicine workstations, doctors can not only conduct consultations, but also perform simple neurological examinations via camera.

The goal:

- faster access to specialist diagnostics
- avoidance of unnecessary hospital stays
 - Better and more continuous care, even for chronic conditions

There are customized solutions, especially for patients with limited mobility, such as tele-home assessment for Parkinson's patients.

The project is being scientifically monitored to determine whether this form of care improves quality of life, reduces hospital admissions, and lowers costs for the healthcare system.
conditions: Demyelinating diseases of the central nervous system
Other degenerative diseases of the nervous system

interventions.name:
TENEAM – Intervention arm (according to TIDieR)

1. Name of the intervention
Teleneurological care (TENEAM).

2. Why (rationale, theory, goal)
Addressing the lack of specialist neurological care close to home in rural areas. Objective: faster neurological assessment, guideline-based diagnostic

Control arm (standard care):
Patients are referred to a private neurology practice by their family doctor as usual and arrange the appointment themselves; further care is provided within the existing structures without additional telemedical support.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
-Unclear neurological symptoms or confirmed neurological diseases requiring specialist neurological assessment or treatment
(e.g., balance disorders, peripheral neuropathies, primary headaches, epilepsy, dementia syndromes, movement disorders, cerebral circulatory disorders, inflammatory CNS syndromes; ; ICD-10 Codes G20-26, G35-37, G30-32, G40-47, G50-54, G56-59, G61.1-G61.9, G62-64, G70-72, H8182, R42, F01, F03)
-No specialist appointment available in the near future and close to home (= no appointment within 3 weeks at a specialist neurological practice within ≤30 min. travel time)
-Legal age (≥ 18 years)
-Written consent to participate in the study and use of routine data
Exclusion criteria:
- Patients receiving care from a family doctor at another practice and referred to the
cooperating practice solely on the basis of a practice substitution
